calls.head: Who blinks first?
calls.body: The Penguins are one of the league’s best for chance quality, but the Golden Knights are one of the best at preventing dangerous shots. We think the Penguins still get theirs.
calls.call: The Penguins’ chances are more dangerous than the league average (a 6.4% chance of scoring on the average shot) against the Golden Knights.

calls.head: Nowhere to hide for Eichel
calls.body: At home, the Penguins keep sending Robertson’s line (Dewar, Lizotte and Robertson) out against opponents’ first lines, far more often than chance would suggest. Dan Muse has been using this group as a checking line on the other team’s top line. Tonight the Golden Knights’ first line is Barbashev, Eichel and Stone.
calls.call: The Penguins’ L4 (Dewar, Lizotte and Robertson) spends at least 52% of its 5-on-5 time against the Golden Knights’ first line, against about 42% with no line matching.
calls.nums: At home: 63% of this group’s 5-on-5 time against first lines, about 42% with no line matching

With no line matching, this group would face first lines about 42% of the time, about as often as those lines are on the ice.

calls.title: Muse got his matchup
calls.plain: Pittsburgh sent Dewar, Lizotte and Robertson out against the Golden Knights’ first line for 55% of their 5-on-5 time, far more than the 42% they’d get with no line matching.
calls.said: Dan Muse would send Dewar, Lizotte and Robertson out against the Golden Knights’ first line again

calls.body: The Golden Knights played last night and get no rest before this one. Teams in that spot usually get the worse of the chances, so we expect the Penguins to control more of the play than they usually do.

surprises.head: Both teams played to type
surprises.body: Nothing in this game strayed far from how these two usually play: the shot share, the quality of chances, special teams, hitting, ice time and goaltending all landed inside their normal night-to-night range.

story.head: Hertl wins it with 35 seconds left
paras: Tomáš Hertl struck first for the Golden Knights on the power play late in the first. The Golden Knights went more than 16 minutes without a shot on goal, from midway through the second to midway through the third, while the Penguins put ten on net. It was a busy third period. Tommy Novak made it 1-1 for Pittsburgh early in the period. Rickard Rakell put the Penguins up 2-1 midway through the period, his fourth straight game with a goal. Trevor Connelly made it 2-2 for Vegas less than two minutes later. Hertl scored his second of the night on the power play with 35 seconds left to put the Golden Knights ahead for good.
The Penguins had a little more of the play, but the Golden Knights had the finish. Adin Hill made 23 saves for the Knights, and Artūrs Šilovs stopped 20 of 23 at the other end.

Jérémy Lauzon took three penalties on his own. The Golden Knights killed all six Penguins power plays. The Golden Knights killed off a two-man advantage that lasted less than two minutes late in the third. The Golden Knights moved to 10-5-2, second in the Pacific, while the Penguins fell to 5-8-2, slipping to seventh in the Metropolitan.
